There was just a brief spell last fall when my mood felt a bit more neutral and I wasn't crying as much, but the lack of interest never really went away.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about that brief period last fall when you felt a bit more neutral, did you experience any significant improvement in your mood or interest in activities during that time, and how did it differ from your current state?\n\nPatient: During that time, I wasn't crying all day and my mood felt a bit more neutral, but it wasn't a real recovery. Even though the heavy sadness lifted slightly, I was still hearing my sister's voice at night and felt convinced the church women were watching me. It was different from now because I wasn't as tearful, but those scary thoughts and voices were still very much present.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about hearing your sister's voice at night and feeling like the church women are watching you, are these experiences still happening to you?\n\nPatient: Yes, it is still happening, and at night I clearly hear my sister calling my name and telling me I'm a burden and should \"come with her.\" I also still know those church ladies are watching me and working with the city to take my house away. These things have been coming and going for most of the past year, even during that spell last fall when my mood felt a bit more neutral.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe more about what you mean by 'knowing' the church ladies are watching you and working against you, is this something you believe is happening in reality or something you recognize as part of your thoughts or feelings?\n\nPatient: No, it is definitely happening in reality, and no matter what my daughter says to try and reassure me, I just know it's real. Those ladies from church who stopped calling after my sister died are constantly talking behind my back and keeping track of what I do. They are working with the hospital and the city to take my house away, and it is just exhausting to deal with.\n\nDoctor: Can you help me understand how these voices and beliefs about the church ladies fit into your daily life, and do you ever have moments where you doubt their reality or think they might be related to your grief or stress?\n\nPatient: I don't doubt them at all because they feel completely real to me, and even though I know my sister is gone, hearing her at night is deeply distressing. Despite what my daughter says, I am absolutely convinced those church ladies are watching me and tracking my actions. These thoughts are usually tangled up with my deep sadness, but even last fall when I wasn't feeling as depressed or crying, I still heard the voices and believed they were watching me for weeks.\n\nDoctor: You've mentioned hearing your sister's voice and believing the church ladies are watching you, can you tell me if you've ever experienced any other unusual perceptions or beliefs that seem real to you, like seeing things that others can't or believing in conspiracies?\n\nPatient: No, I don't see anything that isn't there, and there aren't any other beliefs like that; I just feel too exhausted to even make sense of what I am going through. I'm just so tired all the time now, and I find myself really missing those quiet, peaceful days when my sister and I would just garden and quilt together.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe any other times or situations where you've heard your sister's voice or felt like the church ladies are watching you, and have these experiences been getting worse or more frequent over time?\n\nPatient: I mostly hear my sister's voice late at night when the house is quiet, calling my name or telling me I'm a burden, and I feel the church ladies watching me whenever I'm near the windows. These experiences started a few months after the funeral and have been coming and going for most of the past year. They haven't necessarily gotten worse, but they have stayed a constant, unsettling presence in my life.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if you've ever had times when you weren't hearing your sister's voice or feeling like the church ladies are watching you, and if so, what was different about those times?\n\nPatient: Yes, there have been brief periods where the voices quieted down and I didn't feel like I was being watched. I'm just so tired all the time now, and I find myself really missing those quiet, peaceful days when my sister and I would just garden and quilt together.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe any other times or situations where you've heard your sister's voice or felt like the church ladies are watching you, and have these experiences been getting worse or more frequent over time?\n\nPatient: I mostly hear my sister's voice late at night when the house is quiet, calling my name or telling me I'm a burden, and I feel the church ladies watching me whenever I'm near the windows. I'm just so tired all the time now, and I find myself really missing those quiet, peaceful days when my sister and I would just garden and quilt together.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe any other times or situations where you've heard your sister's voice or felt like the church ladies are watching you, and have these experiences been getting worse or more frequent over time?\n\nPatient: I mostly hear my sister's voice late at night when the house is quiet, calling my name or telling me I'm a burden, and I feel the church ladies watching me whenever I'm near the windows. These experiences started a few months after the funeral and have been coming and going for most of the past year. They haven't necessarily gotten worse, but they have stayed a constant, unsettling presence in my life.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if you've ever had times when you weren't hearing your sister's voice or feeling like the church ladies are watching you, and if so, what was different about those times?\n\nPatient: Yes, there have been brief periods where the voices quieted down and I didn't feel like I was being watched. But even during those times, the only real difference was not having those frightening experiences—the deep, heavy depression and my complete lack of interest in everything were still just as strong.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if you've ever had any moments where you questioned the reality of your sister's voice or the church ladies watching you, or if you've considered the possibility that these experiences might be related to your grief or your mental state?\n\nPatient: With the church ladies, I feel absolutely certain they are watching me and talking behind my back, so I've never really questioned that despite what my daughter says. But hearing my sister's voice does confuse me, because I know deep down she is gone and there is no one else in the house. I've just never really connected either of those things to my grief or my mental state.\n\nDoctor: Can you help me understand how you differentiate between your sister's voice you hear at night and your own thoughts or memories of her, and do you think there's any possibility that these voices could be a manifestation of your grief rather than an actual external voice?\n\nPatient: The voice sounds completely real and external, coming right from the hallway, which feels totally different from just a memory or a thought inside my head. Even though I logically know she is gone and the house is empty, the sound is so clear that it's hard not to take it literally, though I suppose it could be tied to how much I miss her.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if you've ever had any periods where the voices or the belief about the church ladies stopped or significantly decreased, and if so, what triggered that change?\n\nPatient: There have been stretches over the past year where the voices and the feelings about the church ladies quieted down a bit. I honestly don't know what triggered those calmer periods, as they just seemed to happen on their own. Even when they did quiet down, the heavy sadness and emptiness never really left me.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe if there are any specific triggers or events that make the voices or the feelings of being watched worse, or if they seem to happen randomly?\n\nPatient: The voices of my sister are definitely much worse at night when the house gets very quiet and I am left alone with my thoughts. As for the church ladies, that feeling of being watched doesn't really have a specific trigger; it's just a constant, lingering worry that has been there in the background ever since they stopped calling me after the funeral.\n\nDoctor: Do you think that the voices you hear and the beliefs about the church ladies could be related to your own mind or thoughts, rather than being real external events, and have you considered that these might be symptoms of your grief and depression rather than actual happenings?\n\nPatient: While I know my sister is gone, hearing her voice feels incredibly real and scary, and I am so convinced the church ladies are watching me that it's hard to believe it's just in my head, despite what my daughter says. My sadness and these experiences are deeply tangled together, but it's very difficult for me to see them as just symptoms. They truly feel like real things happening to me.\n\nDoctor: Can you help me understand if you think the voices and beliefs about being watched would go away if your depression and sadness improved, or do you believe they are separate issues?"

It was different from now because I wasn't as tearful, but those scary thoughts and voices were still very much present.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about hearing your sister's voice at night and feeling like the church women are watching you, are these experiences still happening to you?\n\nPatient: Yes, it is still happening, and at night I clearly hear my sister calling my name and telling me I'm a burden and should \"come with her.\" I also still know those church ladies are watching me and working with the city to take my house away. These things have been coming and going for most of the past year, even during that spell last fall when my mood felt a bit more neutral.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe more about what you mean by 'knowing' the church ladies are watching you and working against you, is this something you believe is happening in reality or something you recognize as part of your thoughts or feelings?\n\nPatient: No, it is definitely happening in reality, and no matter what my daughter says to try and reassure me, I just know it's real. Those ladies from church who stopped calling after my sister died are constantly talking behind my back and keeping track of what I do. They are working with the hospital and the city to take my house away, and it is just exhausting to deal with.\n\nDoctor: Can you help me understand how these voices and beliefs about the church ladies fit into your daily life, and do you ever have moments where you doubt their reality or think they might be related to your grief or stress?\n\nPatient: I don't doubt them at all because they feel completely real to me, and even though I know my sister is gone, hearing her at night is deeply distressing. Despite what my daughter says, I am absolutely convinced those church ladies are watching me and tracking my actions. These thoughts are usually tangled up with my deep sadness, but even last fall when I wasn't feeling as depressed or crying, I still heard the voices and believed they were watching me for weeks.\n\nDoctor: You've mentioned hearing your sister's voice and believing the church ladies are watching you, can you tell me if you've ever experienced any other unusual perceptions or beliefs that seem real to you, like seeing things that others can't or believing in conspiracies?\n\nPatient: No, I don't see anything that isn't there, and there aren't any other beliefs like that; I just feel too exhausted to even make sense of what I am going through. I'm just so tired all the time now, and I find myself really missing those quiet, peaceful days when my sister and I would just garden and quilt together.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe any other times or situations where you've heard your sister's voice or felt like the church ladies are watching you, and have these experiences been getting worse or more frequent over time?\n\nPatient: I mostly hear my sister's voice late at night when the house is quiet, calling my name or telling me I'm a burden, and I feel the church ladies watching me whenever I'm near the windows. These experiences started a few months after the funeral and have been coming and going for most of the past year. They haven't necessarily gotten worse, but they have stayed a constant, unsettling presence in my life.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if you've ever had times when you weren't hearing your sister's voice or feeling like the church ladies are watching you, and if so, what was different about those times?\n\nPatient: Yes, there have been brief periods where the voices quieted down and I didn't feel like I was being watched. But even during those times, the only real difference was not having those frightening experiences—the deep, heavy depression and my complete lack of interest in everything were still just as strong.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if you've ever had any moments where you questioned the reality of your sister's voice or the church ladies watching you, or if you've considered the possibility that these experiences might be related to your grief or your mental state?\n\nPatient: With the church ladies, I feel absolutely certain they are watching me and talking behind my back, so I've never really questioned that despite what my daughter says. But hearing my sister's voice does confuse me, because I know deep down she is gone and there is no one else in the house. I've just never really connected either of those things to my grief or my mental state.\n\nDoctor: Can you help me understand how you differentiate between your sister's voice you hear at night and your own thoughts or memories of her, and do you think there's any possibility that these voices could be a manifestation of your grief rather than an actual external voice?\n\nPatient: The voice sounds completely real and external, coming right from the hallway, which feels totally different from just a memory or a thought inside my head. Even though I logically know she is gone and the house is empty, the sound is so clear that it's hard not to take it literally, though I suppose it could be tied to how much I miss her.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if you've ever had any periods where the voices or the belief about the church ladies stopped or significantly decreased, and if so, what triggered that change?\n\nPatient: There have been stretches over the past year where the voices and the feelings about the church ladies quieted down a bit. I honestly don't know what triggered those calmer periods, as they just seemed to happen on their own. Even when they did quiet down, the heavy sadness and emptiness never really left me.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe if there are any specific triggers or events that make the voices or the feelings of being watched worse, or if they seem to happen randomly?\n\nPatient: The voices of my sister are definitely much worse at night when the house gets very quiet and I am left alone with my thoughts. My sadness and these experiences are deeply tangled together, but it's very difficult for me to see them as just symptoms. They truly feel like real things happening to me.\n\nDoctor: Can you help me understand if you think the voices and beliefs about being watched would go away if your depression and sadness improved, or do you believe they are separate issues?\n\nPatient: They really feel like separate issues, even though they are usually tangled together. Even though the heavy sadness lifted slightly during those weeks, I still heard my sister's voice at night and remained convinced that the church women were watching me.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe how your beliefs about the church ladies and hearing your sister's voice relate to your feelings of sadness and depression, and do these experiences seem to be directly connected to your mood or do they seem separate from it?"

Most of the time, the deep sadness and those strange experiences are completely tangled up together. Those ladies from church who stopped calling after my sister died are constantly talking behind my back and keeping track of what I do. They are working with the hospital and the city to take my house away, and it is just exhausting to deal with.\n\nDoctor: Can you help me understand how these voices and beliefs about the church ladies fit into your daily life, and do you ever have moments where you doubt their reality or think they might be related to your grief or stress?\n\nPatient: I don't doubt them at all because they feel completely real to me, and even though I know my sister is gone, hearing her at night is deeply distressing. Despite what my daughter says, I am absolutely convinced those church ladies are watching me and tracking my actions. These thoughts are usually tangled up with my deep sadness, but even last fall when I wasn't feeling as depressed or crying, I still heard the voices and believed they were watching me for weeks.\n\nDoctor: You've mentioned hearing your sister's voice and believing the church ladies are watching you, can you tell me if you've ever experienced any other unusual perceptions or beliefs that seem real to you, like seeing things that others can't or believing in conspiracies?\n\nPatient: No, I don't see anything that isn't there, and there aren't any other beliefs like that; I just feel too exhausted to even make sense of what I am going through. I'm just so tired all the time now, and I find myself really missing those quiet, peaceful days when my sister and I would just garden and quilt together.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe any other times or situations where you've heard your sister's voice or felt like the church ladies are watching you, and have these experiences been getting worse or more frequent over time?\n\nPatient: I mostly hear my sister's voice late at night when the house is quiet, calling my name or telling me I'm a burden, and I feel the church ladies watching me whenever I'm near the windows. These experiences started a few months after the funeral and have been coming and going for most of the past year. They haven't necessarily gotten worse, but they have stayed a constant, unsettling presence in my life.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if you've ever had times when you weren't hearing your sister's voice or feeling like the church ladies are watching you, and if so, what was different about those times?\n\nPatient: Yes, there have been brief periods where the voices quieted down and I didn't feel like I was being watched. But even during those times, the only real difference was not having those frightening experiences—the deep, heavy depression and my complete lack of interest in everything were still just as strong.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if you've ever had any moments where you questioned the reality of your sister's voice or the church ladies watching you, or if you've considered the possibility that these experiences might be related to your grief or your mental state?\n\nPatient: With the church ladies, I feel absolutely certain they are watching me and talking behind my back, so I've never really questioned that despite what my daughter says. But hearing my sister's voice does confuse me, because I know deep down she is gone and there is no one else in the house. I've just never really connected either of those things to my grief or my mental state.\n\nDoctor: Can you help me understand how you differentiate between your sister's voice you hear at night and your own thoughts or memories of her, and do you think there's any possibility that these voices could be a manifestation of your grief rather than an actual external voice?\n\nPatient: The voice sounds completely real and external, coming right from the hallway, which feels totally different from just a memory or a thought inside my head. Even though I logically know she is gone and the house is empty, the sound is so clear that it's hard not to take it literally, though I suppose it could be tied to how much I miss her.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if you've ever had any periods where the voices or the belief about the church ladies stopped or significantly decreased, and if so, what triggered that change?\n\nPatient: There have been stretches over the past year where the voices and the feelings about the church ladies quieted down a bit. My sadness and these experiences are deeply tangled together, but it's very difficult for me to see them as just symptoms. I've just never really connected either of those things to my grief or my mental state.\n\nDoctor: Can you help me understand how you differentiate between your sister's voice you hear at night and your own thoughts or memories of her, and do you think there's any possibility that these voices could be a manifestation of your grief rather than an actual external voice?\n\nPatient: The voice sounds completely real and external, coming right from the hallway, which feels totally different from just a memory or a thought inside my head. Even though I logically know she is gone and the house is empty, the sound is so clear that it's hard not to take it literally, though I suppose it could be tied to how much I miss her.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if you've ever had any periods where the voices or the belief about the church ladies stopped or significantly decreased, and if so, what triggered that change?\n\nPatient: There have been stretches over the past year where the voices and the feelings about the church ladies quieted down a bit. I honestly don't know what triggered those calmer periods, as they just seemed to happen on their own. Even when they did quiet down, the heavy sadness and emptiness never really left me.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe if there are any specific triggers or events that make the voices or the feelings of being watched worse, or if they seem to happen randomly?\n\nPatient: The voices of my sister are definitely much worse at night when the house gets very quiet and I am left alone with my thoughts. As for the church ladies, that feeling of being watched doesn't really have a specific trigger; it's just a constant, lingering worry that has been there in the background ever since they stopped calling me after the funeral.\n\nDoctor: Do you think that the voices you hear and the beliefs about the church ladies could be related to your own mind or thoughts, rather than being real external events, and have you considered that these might be symptoms of your grief and depression rather than actual happenings?\n\nPatient: While I know my sister is gone, hearing her voice feels incredibly real and scary, and I am so convinced the church ladies are watching me that it's hard to believe it's just in my head, despite what my daughter says. My sadness and these experiences are deeply tangled together, but it's very difficult for me to see them as just symptoms. Even though I know my sister is gone, her voice and the feeling that the church ladies are watching me feel incredibly real, so I can't just dismiss them as tricks of my mind.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if you've ever had any moments where you felt like the voices or the beliefs about the church ladies were not real, or if you've ever considered seeking help for these specific experiences?"

That was about a year and a half ago, and I've felt this way almost constantly ever since. It just hasn't let up at all.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any periods of significant improvement in your mood or interest in activities since your sister passed away, or has it been a consistent feeling of losing interest over the past year and a half?\n\nPatient: It has been almost constant, and this heavy, joyless feeling has been with me nearly the entire time. There was just a brief spell last fall when my mood felt a bit more neutral and I wasn't crying as much, but the lack of interest never really went away.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about that brief period last fall when you felt a bit more neutral, did you experience any significant improvement in your mood or interest in activities during that time, and how did it differ from your current state?\n\nPatient: During that time, I wasn't crying all day and my mood felt a bit more neutral, but it wasn't a real recovery. Even though the heavy sadness lifted slightly, I was still hearing my sister's voice at night and felt convinced the church women were watching me. It was different from now because I wasn't as tearful, but those scary thoughts and voices were still very much present.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about hearing your sister's voice at night and feeling like the church women are watching you, are these experiences still happening to you?\n\nPatient: Yes, it is still happening, and at night I clearly hear my sister calling my name and telling me I'm a burden and should \"come with her.\" I also still know those church ladies are watching me and working with the city to take my house away. These things have been coming and going for most of the past year, even during that spell last fall when my mood felt a bit more neutral.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe more about what you mean by 'knowing' the church ladies are watching you and working against you, is this something you believe is happening in reality or something you recognize as part of your thoughts or feelings?\n\nPatient: No, it is definitely happening in reality, and no matter what my daughter says to try and reassure me, I just know it's real. Those ladies from church who stopped calling after my sister died are constantly talking behind my back and keeping track of what I do. They are working with the hospital and the city to take my house away, and it is just exhausting to deal with.\n\nDoctor: Can you help me understand how these voices and beliefs about the church ladies fit into your daily life, and do you ever have moments where you doubt their reality or think they might be related to your grief or stress?\n\nPatient: I don't doubt them at all because they feel completely real to me, and even though I know my sister is gone, hearing her at night is deeply distressing. Despite what my daughter says, I am absolutely convinced those church ladies are watching me and tracking my actions. These thoughts are usually tangled up with my deep sadness, but even last fall when I wasn't feeling as depressed or crying, I still heard the voices and believed they were watching me for weeks.\n\nDoctor: You've mentioned hearing your sister's voice and believing the church ladies are watching you, can you tell me if you've ever experienced any other unusual perceptions or beliefs that seem real to you, like seeing things that others can't or believing in conspiracies?\n\nPatient: No, I don't see anything that isn't there, and there aren't any other beliefs like that; I just feel too exhausted to even make sense of what I am going through. I'm just so tired all the time now, and I find myself really missing those quiet, peaceful days when my sister and I would just garden and quilt together.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe any other times or situations where you've heard your sister's voice or felt like the church ladies are watching you, and have these experiences been getting worse or more frequent over time?\n\nPatient: I mostly hear my sister's voice late at night when the house is quiet, calling my name or telling me I'm a burden, and I feel the church ladies watching me whenever I'm near the windows. These experiences started a few months after the funeral and have been coming and going for most of the past year. They haven't necessarily gotten worse, but they have stayed a constant, unsettling presence in my life.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if you've ever had times when you weren't hearing your sister's voice or feeling like the church ladies are watching you, and if so, what was different about those times?\n\nPatient: Yes, there have been brief periods where the voices quieted down and I didn't feel like I was being watched. But even during those times, the only real difference was not having those frightening experiences—the deep, heavy depression and my complete lack of interest in everything were still just as strong.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if you've ever had any moments where you questioned the reality of your sister's voice or the church ladies watching you, or if you've considered the possibility that these experiences might be related to your grief or your mental state?\n\nPatient: With the church ladies, I feel absolutely certain they are watching me and talking behind my back, so I've never really questioned that despite what my daughter says. But hearing my sister's voice does confuse me, because I know deep down she is gone and there is no one else in the house. I've just never really connected either of those things to my grief or my mental state.\n\nDoctor: Can you help me understand how you differentiate between your sister's voice you hear at night and your own thoughts or memories of her, and do you think there's any possibility that these voices could be a manifestation of your grief rather than an actual external voice?\n\nPatient: The voice sounds completely real and external, coming right from the hallway, which feels totally different from just a memory or a thought inside my head. Even though I logically know she is gone and the house is empty, the sound is so clear that it's hard not to take it literally, though I suppose it could be tied to how much I miss her.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if you've ever had any periods where the voices or the belief about the church ladies stopped or significantly decreased, and if so, what triggered that change?\n\nPatient: There have been stretches over the past year where the voices and the feelings about the church ladies quieted down a bit. I honestly don't know what triggered those calmer periods, as they just seemed to happen on their own. Even when they did quiet down, the heavy sadness and emptiness never really left me.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe if there are any specific triggers or events that make the voices or the feelings of being watched worse, or if they seem to happen randomly?\n\nPatient: The voices of my sister are definitely much worse at night when the house gets very quiet and I am left alone with my thoughts. As for the church ladies, that feeling of being watched doesn't really have a specific trigger; it's just a constant, lingering worry that has been there in the background ever since they stopped calling me after the funeral.\n\nDoctor: Do you think that the voices you hear and the beliefs about the church ladies could be related to your own mind or thoughts, rather than being real external events, and have you considered that these might be symptoms of your grief and depression rather than actual happenings?\n\nPatient: While I know my sister is gone, hearing her voice feels incredibly real and scary, and I am so convinced the church ladies are watching me that it's hard to believe it's just in my head, despite what my daughter says. My sadness and these experiences are deeply tangled together, but it's very difficult for me to see them as just symptoms. They truly feel like real things happening to me.\n\nDoctor: Can you help me understand if you think the voices and beliefs about being watched would go away if your depression and sadness improved, or do you believe they are separate issues?\n\nPatient: They really feel like separate issues, even though they are usually tangled together. Last fall, there was a period when my mood felt a bit lighter and I wasn't crying, but I still clearly heard my sister's voice at night and felt certain the church women were watching me for several weeks. Because of that, I don't think those things would just go away even if my sadness improved.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if you've ever experienced any significant periods where the depressive symptoms, such as the lack of interest in activities and the heavy sadness, improved without the voices and beliefs about the church ladies also improving?\n\nPatient: Yes, that actually happened last fall when my mood felt a bit more neutral and I wasn't crying as much. Even though the heavy sadness lifted slightly during those weeks, I still heard my sister's voice at night and remained convinced that the church women were watching me.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe how your beliefs about the church ladies and hearing your sister's voice relate to your feelings of sadness and depression, and do these experiences seem to be directly connected to your mood or do they seem separate from it?\n\nPatient: Most of the time, the deep sadness and those strange experiences are completely tangled up together. But last fall, there was a period of several weeks where my mood felt more neutral and I wasn't crying, yet I still heard my sister's voice and felt watched. So, while they usually happen together, they also seem like separate things that can happen apart from the heavy depression.\n\nDoctor: Do you think the voices and beliefs about the church ladies would still be present if you were no longer feeling sad and disconnected from activities, or are they closely tied to your mood in a way that if one improves, the other might also?\n\nPatient: I do think they would still be present, because they seem to have a life of their own. Even last fall when my mood was more neutral and I wasn't crying, those voices and the feeling of being watched kept going for weeks. So even though they are usually tangled up together, they can definitely exist completely on their own.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever experienced any episodes where you lost touch with reality, aside from hearing your sister's voice and believing the church ladies are watching you, such as feeling like you're in a different place or time, or having thoughts that aren't your own?\n\nPatient: No, I've never had anything like that happen—I've never felt like I was in a different time or place, and my thoughts are always my own. The only things I experience are hearing my sister's voice and knowing the church ladies are watching me. I don't have any of those other kinds of experiences at all.\n\nDoctor: Do you think the voices and beliefs about the church ladies are related to your sadness and grief, or do they seem like a separate issue that's not directly connected to your mood?\n\nPatient: Most of the time, the sadness and those strange experiences feel very tangled together, since they both started around the same time after losing my sister. However, there was a period last fall when my mood was a bit more neutral and I wasn't crying as much, but I was still hearing her voice and believing the church ladies were watching me for weeks. So they seem connected to my grief, but they can also happen completely on their own.\n\nDoctor: Do you think it's possible that the voices you hear and the beliefs about the church ladies could be a part of your mind's way of coping with the intense sadness and grief you've been feeling since your sister passed away?\n\nPatient: I suppose they started around the same time and feel completely tangled up with my sadness, but it's hard to just call them a coping mechanism. Even though I know my sister is gone, her voice and the feeling that the church ladies are watching me feel incredibly real, so I can't just dismiss them as tricks of my mind.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if you've ever had any moments where you felt like the voices or the beliefs about the church ladies were not real, or if you've ever considered seeking help for these specific experiences?\n\nPatient: Even though I know my sister is gone and hearing her doesn't make logical sense, it still feels completely real and terrifying, and I firmly believe the church ladies are trying to take my house despite what my daughter says. I didn't actually seek help for those things specifically; I only agreed to come here because I felt so empty, had lost all interest in life, and my daughter and pastor urged me to get help.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever had any other experiences like hearing your sister's voice or feeling watched that have made you question what is real and what is not, or have these been the only such experiences for you?\n\nPatient: No, those have been the only experiences of that kind for me. I haven't had any other unusual things happen besides hearing my sister's voice calling my name or telling me to join her, and believing that the ladies from my church are watching me to try and take my house.\n\nDoctor: Do you think that if your sadness and lack of interest in activities improved significantly, the voices and beliefs about the church ladies would also go away, or would they likely remain as separate issues?\n\nPatient: I really think they would remain as separate issues, because they don't seem entirely tied to how sad I am. Last fall, there was a period when my mood felt a bit more neutral and I wasn't crying as much, but I still heard my sister's voice at night and felt sure the church ladies were watching me for weeks.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if you've ever had any experiences where you saw things that weren't there, in addition to hearing your sister's voice and believing the church ladies are watching you?\n\nPatient: No, I have never seen things that aren't there. It just hasn't let up at all.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any periods of significant improvement in your mood or interest in activities since your sister passed away, or has it been a consistent feeling of losing interest over the past year and a half?\n\nPatient: It has been almost constant, and this heavy, joyless feeling has been with me nearly the entire time. There was just a brief spell last fall when my mood felt a bit more neutral and I wasn't crying as much, but the lack of interest never really went away.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about that brief period last fall when you felt a bit more neutral, did you experience any significant improvement in your mood or interest in activities during that time, and how did it differ from your current state?\n\nPatient: During that time, I wasn't crying all day and my mood felt a bit more neutral, but it wasn't a real recovery. Even though the heavy sadness lifted slightly, I was still hearing my sister's voice at night and felt convinced the church women were watching me. It was different from now because I wasn't as tearful, but those scary thoughts and voices were still very much present.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about hearing your sister's voice at night and feeling like the church women are watching you, are these experiences still happening to you?\n\nPatient: Yes, it is still happening, and at night I clearly hear my sister calling my name and telling me I'm a burden and should \"come with her.\" I also still know those church ladies are watching me and working with the city to take my house away. These things have been coming and going for most of the past year, even during that spell last fall when my mood felt a bit more neutral.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe more about what you mean by 'knowing' the church ladies are watching you and working against you, is this something you believe is happening in reality or something you recognize as part of your thoughts or feelings?\n\nPatient: No, it is definitely happening in reality, and no matter what my daughter says to try and reassure me, I just know it's real. Those ladies from church who stopped calling after my sister died are constantly talking behind my back and keeping track of what I do. They are working with the hospital and the city to take my house away, and it is just exhausting to deal with.\n\nDoctor: Can you help me understand how these voices and beliefs about the church ladies fit into your daily life, and do you ever have moments where you doubt their reality or think they might be related to your grief or stress?\n\nPatient: I don't doubt them at all because they feel completely real to me, and even though I know my sister is gone, hearing her at night is deeply distressing. Despite what my daughter says, I am absolutely convinced those church ladies are watching me and tracking my actions. These thoughts are usually tangled up with my deep sadness, but even last fall when I wasn't feeling as depressed or crying, I still heard the voices and believed they were watching me for weeks.\n\nDoctor: You've mentioned hearing your sister's voice and believing the church ladies are watching you, can you tell me if you've ever experienced any other unusual perceptions or beliefs that seem real to you, like seeing things that others can't or believing in conspiracies?\n\nPatient: No, I don't see anything that isn't there, and there aren't any other beliefs like that; I just feel too exhausted to even make sense of what I am going through. I'm just so tired all the time now, and I find myself really missing those quiet, peaceful days when my sister and I would just garden and quilt together.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe any other times or situations where you've heard your sister's voice or felt like the church ladies are watching you, and have these experiences been getting worse or more frequent over time?\n\nPatient: I mostly hear my sister's voice late at night when the house is quiet, calling my name or telling me I'm a burden, and I feel the church ladies watching me whenever I'm near the windows. It was different from now because I wasn't as tearful, but those scary thoughts and voices were still very much present.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about hearing your sister's voice at night and feeling like the church women are watching you, are these experiences still happening to you?\n\nPatient: Yes, it is still happening, and at night I clearly hear my sister calling my name and telling me I'm a burden and should \"come with her.\" I also still know those church ladies are watching me and working with the city to take my house away. These things have been coming and going for most of the past year, even during that spell last fall when my mood felt a bit more neutral.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe more about what you mean by 'knowing' the church ladies are watching you and working against you, is this something you believe is happening in reality or something you recognize as part of your thoughts or feelings?\n\nPatient: No, it is definitely happening in reality, and no matter what my daughter says to try and reassure me, I just know it's real. Those ladies from church who stopped calling after my sister died are constantly talking behind my back and keeping track of what I do. They are working with the hospital and the city to take my house away, and it is just exhausting to deal with.\n\nDoctor: Can you help me understand how these voices and beliefs about the church ladies fit into your daily life, and do you ever have moments where you doubt their reality or think they might be related to your grief or stress?\n\nPatient: I don't doubt them at all because they feel completely real to me, and even though I know my sister is gone, hearing her at night is deeply distressing. Despite what my daughter says, I am absolutely convinced those church ladies are watching me and tracking my actions. These thoughts are usually tangled up with my deep sadness, but even last fall when I wasn't feeling as depressed or crying, I still heard the voices and believed they were watching me for weeks.\n\nDoctor: You've mentioned hearing your sister's voice and believing the church ladies are watching you, can you tell me if you've ever experienced any other unusual perceptions or beliefs that seem real to you, like seeing things that others can't or believing in conspiracies?\n\nPatient: No, I don't see anything that isn't there, and there aren't any other beliefs like that; I just feel too exhausted to even make sense of what I am going through. I'm just so tired all the time now, and I find myself really missing those quiet, peaceful days when my sister and I would just garden and quilt together.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe any other times or situations where you've heard your sister's voice or felt like the church ladies are watching you, and have these experiences been getting worse or more frequent over time?\n\nPatient: I mostly hear my sister's voice late at night when the house is quiet, calling my name or telling me I'm a burden, and I feel the church ladies watching me whenever I'm near the windows. These experiences started a few months after the funeral and have been coming and going for most of the past year. They haven't necessarily gotten worse, but they have stayed a constant, unsettling presence in my life.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if you've ever had times when you weren't hearing your sister's voice or feeling like the church ladies are watching you, and if so, what was different about those times?\n\nPatient: Yes, there have been brief periods where the voices quieted down and I didn't feel like I was being watched. But even during those times, the only real difference was not having those frightening experiences—the deep, heavy depression and my complete lack of interest in everything were still just as strong.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if you've ever had any moments where you questioned the reality of your sister's voice or the church ladies watching you, or if you've considered the possibility that these experiences might be related to your grief or your mental state?\n\nPatient: With the church ladies, I feel absolutely certain they are watching me and talking behind my back, so I've never really questioned that despite what my daughter says. But hearing my sister's voice does confuse me, because I know deep down she is gone and there is no one else in the house. I've just never really connected either of those things to my grief or my mental state.\n\nDoctor: Can you help me understand how you differentiate between your sister's voice you hear at night and your own thoughts or memories of her, and do you think there's any possibility that these voices could be a manifestation of your grief rather than an actual external voice?\n\nPatient: The voice sounds completely real and external, coming right from the hallway, which feels totally different from just a memory or a thought inside my head. Even though I logically know she is gone and the house is empty, the sound is so clear that it's hard not to take it literally, though I suppose it could be tied to how much I miss her.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if you've ever had any periods where the voices or the belief about the church ladies stopped or significantly decreased, and if so, what triggered that change?\n\nPatient: There have been stretches over the past year where the voices and the feelings about the church ladies quieted down a bit. I honestly don't know what triggered those calmer periods, as they just seemed to happen on their own. Even when they did quiet down, the heavy sadness and emptiness never really left me.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe if there are any specific triggers or events that make the voices or the feelings of being watched worse, or if they seem to happen randomly?\n\nPatient: The voices of my sister are definitely much worse at night when the house gets very quiet and I am left alone with my thoughts. As for the church ladies, that feeling of being watched doesn't really have a specific trigger; it's just a constant, lingering worry that has been there in the background ever since they stopped calling me after the funeral.\n\nDoctor: Do you think that the voices you hear and the beliefs about the church ladies could be related to your own mind or thoughts, rather than being real external events, and have you considered that these might be symptoms of your grief and depression rather than actual happenings?\n\nPatient: While I know my sister is gone, hearing her voice feels incredibly real and scary, and I am so convinced the church ladies are watching me that it's hard to believe it's just in my head, despite what my daughter says. My sadness and these experiences are deeply tangled together, but it's very difficult for me to see them as just symptoms. They truly feel like real things happening to me.\n\nDoctor: Can you help me understand if you think the voices and beliefs about being watched would go away if your depression and sadness improved, or do you believe they are separate issues?\n\nPatient: They really feel like separate issues, even though they are usually tangled together. Last fall, there was a period when my mood felt a bit lighter and I wasn't crying, but I still clearly heard my sister's voice at night and felt certain the church women were watching me for several weeks. Because of that, I don't think those things would just go away even if my sadness improved.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if you've ever experienced any significant periods where the depressive symptoms, such as the lack of interest in activities and the heavy sadness, improved without the voices and beliefs about the church ladies also improving?\n\nPatient: Yes, that actually happened last fall when my mood felt a bit more neutral and I wasn't crying as much. Even though the heavy sadness lifted slightly during those weeks, I still heard my sister's voice at night and remained convinced that the church women were watching me.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe how your beliefs about the church ladies and hearing your sister's voice relate to your feelings of sadness and depression, and do these experiences seem to be directly connected to your mood or do they seem separate from it?\n\nPatient: Most of the time, the deep sadness and those strange experiences are completely tangled up together. But last fall, there was a period of several weeks where my mood felt more neutral and I wasn't crying, yet I still heard my sister's voice and felt watched. So, while they usually happen together, they also seem like separate things that can happen apart from the heavy depression.\n\nDoctor: Do you think the voices and beliefs about the church ladies would still be present if you were no longer feeling sad and disconnected from activities, or are they closely tied to your mood in a way that if one improves, the other might also?\n\nPatient: I do think they would still be present, because they seem to have a life of their own. Even last fall when my mood was more neutral and I wasn't crying, those voices and the feeling of being watched kept going for weeks. So even though they are usually tangled up together, they can definitely exist completely on their own.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever experienced any episodes where you lost touch with reality, aside from hearing your sister's voice and believing the church ladies are watching you, such as feeling like you're in a different place or time, or having thoughts that aren't your own?\n\nPatient: No, I've never had anything like that happen—I've never felt like I was in a different time or place, and my thoughts are always my own. The only things I experience are hearing my sister's voice and knowing the church ladies are watching me. I don't have any of those other kinds of experiences at all.\n\nDoctor: Do you think the voices and beliefs about the church ladies are related to your sadness and grief, or do they seem like a separate issue that's not directly connected to your mood?\n\nPatient: Most of the time, the sadness and those strange experiences feel very tangled together, since they both started around the same time after losing my sister. However, there was a period last fall when my mood was a bit more neutral and I wasn't crying as much, but I was still hearing her voice and believing the church ladies were watching me for weeks. So they seem connected to my grief, but they can also happen completely on their own.\n\nDoctor: Do you think it's possible that the voices you hear and the beliefs about the church ladies could be a part of your mind's way of coping with the intense sadness and grief you've been feeling since your sister passed away?\n\nPatient: I suppose they started around the same time and feel completely tangled up with my sadness, but it's hard to just call them a coping mechanism. Even though I know my sister is gone, her voice and the feeling that the church ladies are watching me feel incredibly real, so I can't just dismiss them as tricks of my mind.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if you've ever had any moments where you felt like the voices or the beliefs about the church ladies were not real, or if you've ever considered seeking help for these specific experiences?\n\nPatient: Even though I know my sister is gone and hearing her doesn't make logical sense, it still feels completely real and terrifying, and I firmly believe the church ladies are trying to take my house despite what my daughter says. I didn't actually seek help for those things specifically; I only agreed to come here because I felt so empty, had lost all interest in life, and my daughter and pastor urged me to get help.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever had any other experiences like hearing your sister's voice or feeling watched that have made you question what is real and what is not, or have these been the only such experiences for you?\n\nPatient: No, those have been the only experiences of that kind for me. It just hasn't let up at all.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any periods of significant improvement in your mood or interest in activities since your sister passed away, or has it been a consistent feeling of losing interest over the past year and a half?\n\nPatient: It has been almost constant, and this heavy, joyless feeling has been with me nearly the entire time. There was just a brief spell last fall when my mood felt a bit more neutral and I wasn't crying as much, but the lack of interest never really went away.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about that brief period last fall when you felt a bit more neutral, did you experience any significant improvement in your mood or interest in activities during that time, and how did it differ from your current state?\n\nPatient: During that time, I wasn't crying all day and my mood felt a bit more neutral, but it wasn't a real recovery. Even though the heavy sadness lifted slightly, I was still hearing my sister's voice at night and felt convinced the church women were watching me. It was different from now because I wasn't as tearful, but those scary thoughts and voices were still very much present.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about hearing your sister's voice at night and feeling like the church women are watching you, are these experiences still happening to you?\n\nPatient: Yes, it is still happening, and at night I clearly hear my sister calling my name and telling me I'm a burden and should \"come with her.\" I also still know those church ladies are watching me and working with the city to take my house away. These things have been coming and going for most of the past year, even during that spell last fall when my mood felt a bit more neutral.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe more about what you mean by 'knowing' the church ladies are watching you and working against you, is this something you believe is happening in reality or something you recognize as part of your thoughts or feelings?\n\nPatient: No, it is definitely happening in reality, and no matter what my daughter says to try and reassure me, I just know it's real. Those ladies from church who stopped calling after my sister died are constantly talking behind my back and keeping track of what I do. They are working with the hospital and the city to take my house away, and it is just exhausting to deal with.\n\nDoctor: Can you help me understand how these voices and beliefs about the church ladies fit into your daily life, and do you ever have moments where you doubt their reality or think they might be related to your grief or stress?\n\nPatient: I don't doubt them at all because they feel completely real to me, and even though I know my sister is gone, hearing her at night is deeply distressing. Despite what my daughter says, I am absolutely convinced those church ladies are watching me and tracking my actions. These thoughts are usually tangled up with my deep sadness, but even last fall when I wasn't feeling as depressed or crying, I still heard the voices and believed they were watching me for weeks.\n\nDoctor: You've mentioned hearing your sister's voice and believing the church ladies are watching you, can you tell me if you've ever experienced any other unusual perceptions or beliefs that seem real to you, like seeing things that others can't or believing in conspiracies?\n\nPatient: No, I don't see anything that isn't there, and there aren't any other beliefs like that; I just feel too exhausted to even make sense of what I am going through. There was just a brief spell last fall when my mood felt a bit more neutral and I wasn't crying as much, but the lack of interest never really went away.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about that brief period last fall when you felt a bit more neutral, did you experience any significant improvement in your mood or interest in activities during that time, and how did it differ from your current state?\n\nPatient: During that time, I wasn't crying all day and my mood felt a bit more neutral, but it wasn't a real recovery. Even though the heavy sadness lifted slightly, I was still hearing my sister's voice at night and felt convinced the church women were watching me. It was different from now because I wasn't as tearful, but those scary thoughts and voices were still very much present.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about hearing your sister's voice at night and feeling like the church women are watching you, are these experiences still happening to you?\n\nPatient: Yes, it is still happening, and at night I clearly hear my sister calling my name and telling me I'm a burden and should \"come with her.\" I also still know those church ladies are watching me and working with the city to take my house away. These things have been coming and going for most of the past year, even during that spell last fall when my mood felt a bit more neutral.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe more about what you mean by 'knowing' the church ladies are watching you and working against you, is this something you believe is happening in reality or something you recognize as part of your thoughts or feelings?\n\nPatient: No, it is definitely happening in reality, and no matter what my daughter says to try and reassure me, I just know it's real. Those ladies from church who stopped calling after my sister died are constantly talking behind my back and keeping track of what I do. They are working with the hospital and the city to take my house away, and it is just exhausting to deal with.\n\nDoctor: Can you help me understand how these voices and beliefs about the church ladies fit into your daily life, and do you ever have moments where you doubt their reality or think they might be related to your grief or stress?\n\nPatient: I don't doubt them at all because they feel completely real to me, and even though I know my sister is gone, hearing her at night is deeply distressing. Despite what my daughter says, I am absolutely convinced those church ladies are watching me and tracking my actions. These thoughts are usually tangled up with my deep sadness, but even last fall when I wasn't feeling as depressed or crying, I still heard the voices and believed they were watching me for weeks.\n\nDoctor: You've mentioned hearing your sister's voice and believing the church ladies are watching you, can you tell me if you've ever experienced any other unusual perceptions or beliefs that seem real to you, like seeing things that others can't or believing in conspiracies?\n\nPatient: No, I don't see anything that isn't there, and there aren't any other beliefs like that; I just feel too exhausted to even make sense of what I am going through. I'm just so tired all the time now, and I find myself really missing those quiet, peaceful days when my sister and I would just garden and quilt together.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe any other times or situations where you've heard your sister's voice or felt like the church ladies are watching you, and have these experiences been getting worse or more frequent over time?\n\nPatient: I mostly hear my sister's voice late at night when the house is quiet, calling my name or telling me I'm a burden, and I feel the church ladies watching me whenever I'm near the windows. These experiences started a few months after the funeral and have been coming and going for most of the past year. They haven't necessarily gotten worse, but they have stayed a constant, unsettling presence in my life.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if you've ever had times when you weren't hearing your sister's voice or feeling like the church ladies are watching you, and if so, what was different about those times?\n\nPatient: Yes, there have been brief periods where the voices quieted down and I didn't feel like I was being watched. But even during those times, the only real difference was not having those frightening experiences—the deep, heavy depression and my complete lack of interest in everything were still just as strong.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if you've ever had any moments where you questioned the reality of your sister's voice or the church ladies watching you, or if you've considered the possibility that these experiences might be related to your grief or your mental state?\n\nPatient: With the church ladies, I feel absolutely certain they are watching me and talking behind my back, so I've never really questioned that despite what my daughter says. But hearing my sister's voice does confuse me, because I know deep down she is gone and there is no one else in the house. I've just never really connected either of those things to my grief or my mental state.\n\nDoctor: Can you help me understand how you differentiate between your sister's voice you hear at night and your own thoughts or memories of her, and do you think there's any possibility that these voices could be a manifestation of your grief rather than an actual external voice?\n\nPatient: The voice sounds completely real and external, coming right from the hallway, which feels totally different from just a memory or a thought inside my head. Even though I logically know she is gone and the house is empty, the sound is so clear that it's hard not to take it literally, though I suppose it could be tied to how much I miss her.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if you've ever had any periods where the voices or the belief about the church ladies stopped or significantly decreased, and if so, what triggered that change?\n\nPatient: There have been stretches over the past year where the voices and the feelings about the church ladies quieted down a bit. I honestly don't know what triggered those calmer periods, as they just seemed to happen on their own. Even when they did quiet down, the heavy sadness and emptiness never really left me.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe if there are any specific triggers or events that make the voices or the feelings of being watched worse, or if they seem to happen randomly?\n\nPatient: The voices of my sister are definitely much worse at night when the house gets very quiet and I am left alone with my thoughts. As for the church ladies, that feeling of being watched doesn't really have a specific trigger; it's just a constant, lingering worry that has been there in the background ever since they stopped calling me after the funeral.\n\nDoctor: Do you think that the voices you hear and the beliefs about the church ladies could be related to your own mind or thoughts, rather than being real external events, and have you considered that these might be symptoms of your grief and depression rather than actual happenings?\n\nPatient: While I know my sister is gone, hearing her voice feels incredibly real and scary, and I am so convinced the church ladies are watching me that it's hard to believe it's just in my head, despite what my daughter says. My sadness and these experiences are deeply tangled together, but it's very difficult for me to see them as just symptoms. They truly feel like real things happening to me.\n\nDoctor: Can you help me understand if you think the voices and beliefs about being watched would go away if your depression and sadness improved, or do you believe they are separate issues?\n\nPatient: They really feel like separate issues, even though they are usually tangled together. Last fall, there was a period when my mood felt a bit lighter and I wasn't crying, but I still clearly heard my sister's voice at night and felt certain the church women were watching me for several weeks. Because of that, I don't think those things would just go away even if my sadness improved.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if you've ever experienced any significant periods where the depressive symptoms, such as the lack of interest in activities and the heavy sadness, improved without the voices and beliefs about the church ladies also improving?\n\nPatient: Yes, that actually happened last fall when my mood felt a bit more neutral and I wasn't crying as much. Even though the heavy sadness lifted slightly during those weeks, I still heard my sister's voice at night and remained convinced that the church women were watching me.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe how your beliefs about the church ladies and hearing your sister's voice relate to your feelings of sadness and depression, and do these experiences seem to be directly connected to your mood or do they seem separate from it?\n\nPatient: Most of the time, the deep sadness and those strange experiences are completely tangled up together. But last fall, there was a period of several weeks where my mood felt more neutral and I wasn't crying, yet I still heard my sister's voice and felt watched. So, while they usually happen together, they also seem like separate things that can happen apart from the heavy depression.\n\nDoctor: Do you think the voices and beliefs about the church ladies would still be present if you were no longer feeling sad and disconnected from activities, or are they closely tied to your mood in a way that if one improves, the other might also?\n\nPatient: I do think they would still be present, because they seem to have a life of their own. Even last fall when my mood was more neutral and I wasn't crying, those voices and the feeling of being watched kept going for weeks. So even though they are usually tangled up together, they can definitely exist completely on their own.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever experienced any episodes where you lost touch with reality, aside from hearing your sister's voice and believing the church ladies are watching you, such as feeling like you're in a different place or time, or having thoughts that aren't your own?\n\nPatient: No, I've never had anything like that happen—I've never felt like I was in a different time or place, and my thoughts are always my own. The only things I experience are hearing my sister's voice and knowing the church ladies are watching me. I don't have any of those other kinds of experiences at all.\n\nDoctor: Do you think the voices and beliefs about the church ladies are related to your sadness and grief, or do they seem like a separate issue that's not directly connected to your mood?\n\nPatient: Most of the time, the sadness and those strange experiences feel very tangled together, since they both started around the same time after losing my sister. However, there was a period last fall when my mood was a bit more neutral and I wasn't crying as much, but I was still hearing her voice and believing the church ladies were watching me for weeks. So they seem connected to my grief, but they can also happen completely on their own.\n\nDoctor: Do you think it's possible that the voices you hear and the beliefs about the church ladies could be a part of your mind's way of coping with the intense sadness and grief you've been feeling since your sister passed away?\n\nPatient: I suppose they started around the same time and feel completely tangled up with my sadness, but it's hard to just call them a coping mechanism. Even though I know my sister is gone, her voice and the feeling that the church ladies are watching me feel incredibly real, so I can't just dismiss them as tricks of my mind.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if you've ever had any moments where you felt like the voices or the beliefs about the church ladies were not real, or if you've ever considered seeking help for these specific experiences?\n\nPatient: Even though I know my sister is gone and hearing her doesn't make logical sense, it still feels completely real and terrifying, and I firmly believe the church ladies are trying to take my house despite what my daughter says. I didn't actually seek help for those things specifically; I only agreed to come here because I felt so empty, had lost all interest in life, and my daughter and pastor urged me to get help.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever had any other experiences like hearing your sister's voice or feeling watched that have made you question what is real and what is not, or have these been the only such experiences for you?\n\nPatient: No, those have been the only experiences of that kind for me. I haven't had any other unusual things happen besides hearing my sister's voice calling my name or telling me to join her, and believing that the ladies from my church are watching me to try and take my house.\n\nDoctor: Do you think that if your sadness and lack of interest in activities improved significantly, the voices and beliefs about the church ladies would also go away, or would they likely remain as separate issues?\n\nPatient: I really think they would remain as separate issues, because they don't seem entirely tied to how sad I am.
